hypotheses.economic_prior: At each 8h settlement, longs mechanically pay shorts (or vice versa). When positive funding is extreme, the mechanical payment creates a temporary sell wall as longs hedge, reduce, or close positions. Unlike funding-rate DIRECTIONAL (killed H-003) or funding-CARRY (killed), this is a TIMING hypothesis: the settlement time is FIXED and PUBLIC. The causal direction is regime-invariant: a 0.01% positive funding rate ALWAYS transfers 0.01% from longs to shorts at settlement. This is a friction-cost harvest, not a directional bet. The mechanism is bounded by its own constraint: if the effect were too predictable, arbitrageurs would front-run it, but the 30-60s system latency means front-running by THIS system is on the correct side (settle T+0 re-entry is not front-running).

result.evidence: 21,900 real 8h funding cycles across 10 liquid Binance USDT-M perps (2,190 per symbol = full 2 years at 3 cycles/day), fetched via paginated startTime/endTime fapi calls (the single fundingRate call caps at ~1000 rows). The delta-neutral book always positions on the PAID side of funding (short perp when funding>0, long perp when funding<0) and only holds a cycle when gross funding clears the per-cycle running cost. TWO-GATE result: Gate (b) HARNESS PASSES - the per-cycle net-carry series is stably admissible (13 strong windows, all same-sign positive, eff +1.69..+3.86) because by construction held cycles always have net>0. Per-cycle running cost ~2.05bp (amortised round-trip 4-fill fees+slippage over a 30-cycle hold + 6%/yr borrow + rehedge drag) is LARGER than the typical 8h funding rate for liquid majors (~0.7bp median). Only 740 of 21,900 cycles (3.4%) had funding large enough to clear costs; across the full opportunity set the cost model eats 94% of the gross funding. This is the well-documented reason retail funding-arb does not work at retail fee tiers: the contractual carry is real but thin, and round-trip taker costs dominate it.
result.data_caveat: Costs are a harsh-but-fair retail model (Binance 5bp perp / 10bp spot taker, 1.5bp half-spread slippage per fill, 6%/yr short-leg borrow). A maker-rebate or VIP-tier fee schedule, or a longer hold that amortises entry/exit further, would lift survival - but the per-cycle borrow + rehedge drag alone (~0.6bp) still consumes a large share of median funding. The harness PASS on gate (b) is a construction artifact (held cycles are net-positive by definition), not an independent edge confirmation - the cost-survival gate is the binding constraint here.

mining_difficulty_lag_2026_05_19.description: BTC hash-rate vs the ~2-week difficulty-retarget lag. Bitcoin difficulty re-targets every 2016 blocks (~14 days); between retargets, hash-rate drifts freely while the difficulty number is frozen. The GAP between current hash-rate and the hash-rate implied by the last difficulty setting is a miner-economics signal: when hash-rate has risen well above the level the standing difficulty was set for, blocks are being found fast, miner revenue-per-hash is elevated, and the NEXT retarget will raise difficulty (a known forward cost shock to miners); when hash-rate has fallen below it, the next retarget cuts difficulty. SIGNAL on day D: hashrate_gap_D = (avg_hashrate_D / hashrate_at_last_retarget) - 1, standardised to a z-score against a strictly-past trailing 180-day window of the same gap series (D excluded). Economic direction: a large POSITIVE gap (hash-rate far above the retarget baseline) precedes an upward difficulty adjustment that squeezes marginal miner margins and historically coincides with miners pre-emptively selling BTC into strength -> SHORT BTC over the next 5 days; a large NEGATIVE gap precedes a downward adjustment / capitulation bottom -> LONG. Continuous daily-position book on BTC; harness score field signal_z = |hashrate_gap_z|, the conviction magnitude.

h040_equity_sector_momentum.description: EQUITY industry/sector cross-sectional momentum signal (Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999, Do Industries Explain Momentum?). Universe: the 11 SPDR sector ETFs — XLB (materials), XLE (energy), XLF (financials), XLI (industrials), XLK (technology), XLP (consumer staples), XLU (utilities), XLV (health care), XLY (consumer discretionary), XLRE (real estate), XLC (communication services) — the GICS sector partition of the US large-cap market. At every monthly rebalance date D: momentum_i(D) = close_i(D) / close_i(D-21) - 1; rank sectors cross-sectionally; LONG the TOP-2, SHORT the BOTTOM-2; equal-weight long-short basket held until the next monthly rebalance (~21 trading days). Optional trend filter (pre-registered ON): the book sits FLAT unless SPY is above its 252-day (12-month) moving average at the rebalance date — the regime guard for bear markets where cross-sectional dispersion narrows and the momentum spread inverts. signal_z = |cross-sectional momentum z-score| of the picked sector vs the 11-sector cross-section on the rebalance date (conviction magnitude; harness score field |signal_z|). Tested as a FULL continuous-position long-short book — every (picked_sector, held_day) with a next bar is one resolved record, NO selection of big momentum moves, NO post-hoc |z| threshold — the legitimate H-008/H-019/H-026/H-027 density construction. STRICT no-look-ahead: 21d momentum at D uses closes strictly through D; entry on the bar AFTER D; the 252d SPY MA is end-anchored at D over the trailing window. Turnover-aware cost: a single 15bps round-trip is charged on the FIRST held day of each rebalance period (in + out across the period), not per-day.
